title: Ensure excessive administrative privileges are revoked
query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper = true;
rationale: Only authorized database administrators should possess superuser privileges. Excessive administrative privileges increase the impact of compromised accounts.
remediation: Review all PostgreSQL superuser roles and revoke unnecessary SUPERUSER privileges using ALTER ROLE.

title: Ensure excessive function privileges are revoked
rationale: Functions capable of executing privileged operations should only be executable by authorized roles.
remediation: Review EXECUTE privileges on user-defined functions and revoke unnecessary permissions using REVOKE EXECUTE.

title: Ensure excessive DML privileges are revoked
rationale: Data modification privileges should be granted only to roles that require them.
remediation: Review INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE privileges on all application objects and revoke unnecessary access.

title: Ensure Row Level Security (RLS) is configured correctly
query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_class WHERE relrowsecurity = true;
rationale: Row Level Security restricts access to individual rows based on security policies.
remediation: Enable Row Level Security on tables that require row-based access control using ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

title: Ensure the set_user extension is installed
rationale: The set_user extension provides controlled privilege escalation for administrative operations.
remediation: Install the set_user extension and configure it according to organizational security requirements.

title: Make use of predefined roles
rationale: Using PostgreSQL predefined roles simplifies privilege management and reduces administrative errors.
remediation: Review role assignments and use PostgreSQL predefined roles wherever applicable instead of granting individual privileges.
